title: Slot Pattern
description: Learn how to use the slot pattern to create flexible, composable components that accept arbitrary content at named injection points.

data.text: The slot pattern is a composition technique where a parent component defines named regions—called slots—that consumers fill with arbitrary content. This concept originates from web components and Angular content projection, but in React it is implemented using props.children, named children props, or render functions. Slots let you build highly reusable layout and container components while giving downstream developers full control over what renders inside each region.

data.title: Why Slots Matter
data.text: Without slots, you either bake every possible variation into a prop explosion or force consumers to wrap your component in awkward extra elements. Slots give you the best of both worlds: a stable outer shell with customizable inner regions.

React's props.children gives you a single unnamed default slot. To create named slots, you can pass additional render props or use a single composition object. Each slot receives exactly the data it needs to render independently. The parent component orchestrates layout and context, while each slot focuses only on its own content.

terms.definition: The unnamed children prop that renders inside the primary content area of a component.
A labeled content region, such as header, sidebar, or footer, passed via a dedicated prop or composition object.
The act of passing JSX from a consumer into a component so the component decides where to render it.
Data passed from the parent down into each slot's render function, enabling slots to access context or state.
A single prop whose keys map to slot names and whose values are ReactNode or render functions, grouping multiple slots into one declarative argument.

data.text: A Card component is a classic example. It has a header, body, and footer region. Instead of relying on consumers to nest separate Header, Body, and Footer components manually, you define one Card component with named slot props. This keeps JSX clean and prevents invalid nesting.

data.title: Card Component with Named Slots
data.content: A Card component that accepts header, body, and footer slots as separate props.

data.text: Use short-circuit evaluation when rendering slots. This prevents empty wrapper elements from appearing when a slot is not provided.

Sometimes a slot needs data from the parent component, such as loading state, error messages, or pagination controls. In those cases, the slot should be a function that receives the data as an argument. This is the render-prop variant of the slot pattern. It gives the slot full control over how to use the data without tightly coupling the child to the parent's state shape.

data.title: DataList with Render Prop Slots
data.content: A list component that passes item data, loading state, and error information into slot render functions.

data.caption: The slot pattern separates a parent's layout shell from the consumer's content.
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[Parent Component] -->|passes| B[Slot: header]
    A -->|passes| C[Slot: body]
    A -->|passes| D[Slot: footer]
    B -->|renders inside| E[Component Shell]
    C -->|renders inside| E
    D -->|renders inside| E
    E -->|outputs| F[Composed UI]

data.text: For components with many slots, a single composition-object prop can be cleaner than many individual props. You define a type that maps slot names to ReactNode or render functions, and the component iterates over the object to render each slot in its designated region. This pattern scales well when the number of slots is dynamic or when you want to support custom slot registration.

data.content: A dashboard layout that accepts a single slots object containing header, sidebar, main, and footer.

cards.title: props.children
cards.description: Use a single default slot for the main content area.

cards.title: Named Props
cards.description: Declare each slot as a separate optional prop.
cons: Can feel verbose with many slots

cards.title: Composition Object
cards.description: Pass a single object mapping slot names to content.

cards.title: Render Props
cards.description: Pass functions as slots to receive parent data.
cons: Can overfit if data shape changes

data.title: Exercise: Build a Card Component with Named Slots
data.description: Create a Card component that accepts header, body, and footer named slots. The component should render each slot inside a distinctly styled region and gracefully handle missing slots.
steps: Define a CardSlots type with optional header, body, and footer props of type ReactNode.
Render the header inside a styled div, the body inside the main content area, and the footer at the bottom.
Use short-circuit evaluation so empty slots do not produce empty DOM elements.
Add a named-slot prop for an optional 'action' region and render it in the header next to the title.
Consume the component by passing JSX to each slot and verify the layout holds.
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable Card component where consumers can inject custom content into named regions without touching the component's internal layout logic.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The slot pattern lets consumers inject content into named regions of a component.
Use props.children for the default slot and additional props for named slots.
Render props turn slots into functions that receive data from the parent.
A composition object groups all slots into a single prop, which scales better for large components.
Named slots prevent prop drilling and keep JSX clean when a component has multiple customizable regions.
data.takeaway: Slots shift control from the component author to the component consumer, making layouts reusable without sacrificing flexibility.
